about: The Ultimate Challenge's own rounds: the topic's target words in new sentences, never shown on its pages, Boards or in Defuse.

rounds.prompt: Hundreds of students took ___ in the climate march.
rounds.note: take part in = join in an activity. Take place means 'happen'.

rounds.prompt: Please keep this medicine out of ___ of children.
rounds.note: out of reach = too far away to get to.

rounds.prompt: She ___ her voice so that she wouldn't wake the baby.
rounds.note: You lower your voice; reduce and decrease are for amounts and prices.

rounds.prompt: It would be ___ to take an umbrella — it looks like rain.
rounds.note: sensible = showing good judgement; sensitive = easily affected.

rounds.prompt: She ___ into tears when she heard the news.
rounds.note: burst into tears = suddenly start crying.

rounds.prompt: He's a ___ millionaire who left school at sixteen.
rounds.note: self-made = rich through your own work.

rounds.prompt: Prices ___ a lot from one shop to another.
rounds.note: vary = be different from one case to another.

rounds.prompt: The lift is ___, so we'll have to take the stairs.
rounds.note: out of order = not working.

rounds.prompt: The doctor told him to take one ___ of the medicine every morning.
rounds.note: a dose = the amount of medicine taken at one time.

rounds.prompt: Always read the ___ on the bottle before you take any medicine.
rounds.note: the label = the piece of paper on a product with information.

rounds.prompt: She was ___ head of the science department last year.
rounds.note: be appointed = be chosen for a job or position.

rounds.prompt: He gave his grandmother a ___ of flowers for her birthday.
rounds.note: a bunch of flowers.

rounds.prompt: That face looks ___ — have we met before?
rounds.note: familiar = known to you; accustomed to = used to.

rounds.prompt: She ___ the house from her grandfather when he died.
rounds.note: inherit = receive from someone who has died.

rounds.prompt: This screw is ___ — can you tighten it, please?
rounds.note: loose (adjective) = not tight; lose (verb) = not find.

rounds.prompt: The main ___ of the heart is to pump blood around the body.
rounds.note: function = the job something does.

rounds.prompt: I deeply ___ not telling her the truth.
rounds.note: regret + -ing = be sorry you did or didn't do it.

rounds.prompt: She ___ her head to show that she disagreed.
rounds.note: shake your head = no; nod = yes.

rounds.prompt: Good luck tomorrow — I'll keep my ___ crossed for you!
rounds.note: keep your fingers crossed = hope for good luck.

rounds.prompt: It doesn't ___ if you're a few minutes late.
rounds.note: it doesn't matter = it isn't important.

rounds.prompt: The doctor decided to ___ him to a specialist.
rounds.note: refer someone to = send them for help.

rounds.prompt: After years of temporary jobs, she finally has a ___ income.
rounds.note: a steady income = regular and reliable.

rounds.prompt: The weather ___ says it will snow tomorrow.
rounds.note: the weather forecast (noun).

rounds.prompt: If you ___ these instructions carefully, you can't go wrong.
rounds.note: follow instructions.

rounds.prompt: The plane landed safely on the ___ despite the strong wind.
rounds.note: the runway = where planes land and take off.

rounds.prompt: The class went on a school ___ to the science museum.
rounds.note: an outing = a short trip for pleasure.

rounds.prompt: She's been working ___ every evening to finish the project.
rounds.note: work overtime = extra hours.

rounds.prompt: Someone has ___ mud all over the kitchen floor.
rounds.note: tread mud into / over something; trodden is the past participle.

rounds.prompt: Which page are you ___ to?
rounds.note: refer to = talk about; mention takes no 'to'.

rounds.prompt: Stand on your ___ so you can see over the crowd.
rounds.note: stand on your toes = stand as tall as possible.
